name: Plane Jacobian conjecture
question: Does a polynomial map C² to C² with constant nonzero Jacobian have a polynomial inverse?
dispatch_next: Do not enumerate degree-4 maps with coefficients in {-1,0,1}: Moh (1983) already covers plane maps of degree at most 100. Name one Newton-polygon family outside that degree bound and state the coefficient ring before any search.
dispatch_why: Moh (1983) covers plane maps of degree at most 100. Degree-4 search on coefficients in {-1,0,1} sits inside that theorem, so the recorded experiment is refused.

campaign.method: Exhaustive integer plane maps with inverses certified under Gabber's degree bound
campaign.hypothesis: Every polynomial map C^2 -> C^2 with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant has a polynomial inverse.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Reproduce the classical low-degree cases (Wang: degree <= 2; Moh: plane degree <= 100) on exhaustive integer classes, then isolate a structured family, such as maps with a prescribed Newton polygon, not covered by known degree bounds.
campaign.next_experiment: Enlarge the class to degree 4 with coefficients in {-1,0,1} using kernel enumeration per monomial support, and record the distribution of inverse degrees and of tame decompositions.
campaign.falsification: A plane map with exactly verified constant nonzero Jacobian and an exact proof (an infeasible linear system under Gabber's bound) that no inverse of degree <= deg F exists.
campaign.blocker: Known results already cover plane maps of degree <= 100, so exhaustive small classes cannot reach new territory; novelty needs structural families.

probes.name: Plane Jacobian conjecture
probes.title: Plane Jacobian conjecture on exhaustive classes of small integer polynomial maps
probes.frontier: Known: true for plane maps of degree <= 100 (Moh 1983) and in degree <= 2 in every dimension (Wang 1980); open in general. Reproduction only.

smoke.scope: Every plane map (f, g) with deg <= 2, zero constant terms and coefficients in {-1, 0, 1} whose Jacobian is a nonzero constant has an explicit polynomial inverse of degree <= 2.

deep.scope: Every plane map (f, g) with deg <= 3, zero constant terms and coefficients in {-1, 0, 1} whose Jacobian is a nonzero constant has an explicit polynomial inverse of degree <= 3.

milestones.title: Plane Jacobian conjecture verified on all 59,049 integer maps of degree <= 2 with coefficients in {-1,0,1}
milestones.description: 240 maps have constant nonzero Jacobian (matching brute force); each has an explicit inverse of degree <= 2 checked by composition in both orders, and completeness is re-derived from a separate evaluation-based linear system. The deep run covers all 387,420,489 maps of degree <= 3 (816 with constant Jacobian), every one inverted.
